question: Why can a geo-stationary satellite monitor the movement of clouds accurately?

options.text: Because it moves in North to South direction.
Because it moves in South to North direction.
Because it is stationary relative to any place on Earth.
Because it rotates faster than Earth.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Because it is stationary relative to any place on Earth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A **geo-stationary satellite** orbits the Earth at the same rotational speed as the Earth itself. Hence, it appears stationary when observed from any point on the Earth's surface. This is why it can monitor cloud movements accurately.
 
• It is positioned in a geosynchronous orbit, approximately **35,786 kilometers above the Earth's equator**. This specific altitude ensures its synchronization with Earth's rotation.
 
• Since the satellite remains fixed relative to a specific location on Earth, it provides a continuous and consistent view of the same
